title: Guide: two clauses from one counterexample
description: The check finds up to two surviving cliques in one answer set and writes one clause for each with clause/3; a #heuristic, honoured because of --heuristic=Domain, makes it look for the second. See the guide page "Getting more out of each check".

fragments.name: shared
fragments.text:
% The Paley graph on n nodes (n a prime of the form 4m + 1): two nodes are joined when
% their difference is a square modulo n.
node(0..n-1).
square((X*X) \ n) :- X = 1..n-1.
edge(U,V) :- node(U), node(V), U < V, square((V-U) \ n).
fragments.description: The Paley graph on n nodes. Added to every solver.

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.text:
% A candidate: at most k nodes to delete.
{ del(V) : node(V) } k.
#show del/1.
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): at most k deleted nodes.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.text:
% The check sees which nodes are deleted.
glue(del(V)) :- node(V).
fragments.description: The interface atoms: the deleted nodes.

fragments.name: check
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: clique 1, c nodes that are not deleted and pairwise joined;
% if possible a second one, clique 2, that differs from it.
clique(1). { clique(2) }.
#heuristic clique(2). [1,true]
c { q(I,V) : node(V) } c :- clique(I).
:- q(I,V), del(V).
:- q(I,U), q(I,V), U < V, not edge(U,V).
:- clique(2), q(2,V) : q(1,V).
#show q/2.

% One clause per clique: one of its nodes must be deleted.
clause(I, del(V), true) :- q(I,V).
fragments.description: Looks for up to two surviving cliques and writes one clause per clique (solver C).

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# The check derives the clauses itself: clause(Id, Atom, Value).
search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clauses(X)
